Parallel, founded by ex-Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal, has secured $100 million to build a new kind of web infrastructure. The system is not for people. It is for artificial intelligence.

Some funds will also go into addressing paywalls and login barriers that block AI systems from gathering web data. Agrawal said content lockouts are becoming a big challenge. Many publishers are blocking web crawlers to stop AI companies from scraping their data. Parallel plans to build what Agrawal called an “open market mechanism.” The idea is to pay or credit content owners when their pages are used by AI agents. If the model succeeds, it could reshape how information is shared online.
